exports.name: SCREEN_W
exports.doc: Native Orion viewport width (`160` `px`, equivalent to `10` `tiles` at `16` `px` per tile).

exports.name: SCREEN_H
exports.doc: Native Orion viewport height (`144` `px`, equivalent to `9` `tiles` at `16` `px` per tile).

exports.name: TILE_SIZE
exports.doc: World grid tile dimension (`16` `px` square).

exports.name: COLS
exports.doc: Default single-screen room width in tiles (`10` `tiles` = `160` `px`).

exports.name: ROWS
exports.doc: Default single-screen room height in tiles (`9` `tiles` = `144` `px`).

exports.name: RoomDimensions
exports.doc: Resolved grid dimensions (`cols`, `rows` in `tiles`) and pixel bounds (`widthPx`, `heightPx` in `px`) for a room.

exports.name: getRoomDimensions
exports.doc: Computes the tile (`cols`, `rows`) and pixel (`widthPx`, `heightPx`) dimensions of `roomGrid`, defaulting to `10 x 9` (`160x144` `px`).

exports.name: VisibleTileBounds
exports.doc: Camera-clamped inclusive tile index window (`minTx..maxTx`, `minTy..maxTy`) for viewport culling.

exports.name: getVisibleTileBounds
exports.doc: Computes the camera-clamped visible tile coordinate window `[minTx..maxTx, minTy..maxTy]` so rendering passes run in O(viewport) time even in 100x90 (10x10 screen) rooms.

exports.name: getRoomDoorwayCenterPx
exports.doc: Locates the open doorway span and center pixel coordinates along a cardinal wall of `roomGrid`. Falls back to proportional center coordinates if the wall has no carved opening.

exports.name: Z_SCALE
exports.doc: Vertical 2.5D projection factor (`1.0` `px` per `z` unit) converting elevation `z` into screen-space `Y` offset.

exports.name: PERFECT_BLOCK_WINDOW_SEC
exports.doc: Duration in seconds (`0.34` `s`) after raising a shield during which incoming hits trigger a Perfect Block (`mechanics-v1.md §5`).

exports.name: WEAPON_SWAP_COOLDOWN
exports.doc: Cooldown in seconds (`5.0` `s`) enforced between auxiliary weapon swaps.

exports.name: BOOSTER_DASH_DURATION
exports.doc: Active impulse duration in seconds (`0.20` `s`) of a booster evade dash.

exports.name: BOOSTER_DASH_COOLDOWN
exports.doc: Recovery cooldown in seconds (`0.75` `s`) between consecutive booster dashes.

exports.name: BOOSTER_HEAT_COST
exports.doc: Reactor heat generated (`22` heat units) when triggering a booster dash.

exports.name: WALK_SPEED
exports.doc: Base mech ground movement speed (`44` `px/s`, or `2.75` `tiles/s`).

exports.name: MUD_SPEED_PENALTY
exports.doc: Movement speed multiplier (`0.65`) applied when wading through mire or mud terrain tiles.

exports.name: BOOSTER_SPEED
exports.doc: Peak ground velocity (`124` `px/s`) applied during an active booster dash.

exports.name: JUMP_VELOCITY
exports.doc: Initial vertical jump impulse (`175` `px/s` along the `z` axis).

exports.name: GRAVITY
exports.doc: Downward vertical acceleration (`560` `px/s²` along the `z` axis) applied while airborne.

exports.name: COLOR_SHIELD

exports.name: COLOR_ARMOR

exports.name: COLOR_CRITICAL

exports.name: COLOR_HEAT
exports.doc: Canonical HUD and telemetry hex color (`#f97316`) for Reactor Heat warnings.

exports.name: DIR_VECTORS
exports.doc: Normalized 2D unit vectors (`x`, `y`) for all 8 canonical `OrionDir` compass directions (`N`, `NE`, `E`, `SE`, `S`, `SW`, `W`, `NW`).

exports.name: getDirFromVector
exports.doc: Quantizes a 2D movement or aim vector `(dx, dy)` into the nearest 8-way `OrionDir` compass direction.

exports.name: AETHER_PYRAMID_DEPTHS
exports.doc: Canonical Æther Fog depth tiers (`1..4`) mapping distance from the Set Path to procedural room complexity.

exports.name: KeyNodeRouteDescriptor
exports.doc: Route metadata describing a canonical Set Path key room (`coord`, `title`, `exitDir`, `nextKeyCoord`).

exports.name: KEY_NODE_ROUTES
exports.doc: Ordered progression spine mapping Set Path room coordinates (`"0,0"` through `"5,0"`) to their `KeyNodeRouteDescriptor`.

exports.name: deterministicAetherHash
exports.doc: Computes a deterministic 32-bit unsigned integer hash from a string seed for procedural Æther room and chunk generation.

exports.name: getKeyBorderBranchType
exports.doc: Determines whether exiting `coord` along `dir` leads along the Set Path (`'key'`), into a loop, or into an Æther Fog branch.

exports.name: hasPoeLanternGuidance
exports.doc: Returns `true` when the pilot has earned Poe's spectral lantern guidance (`poe_state === 'helped'` or `'companion'`).

exports.name: resolveCompanionPoeColor
exports.doc: Resolves the Companion Poe orb's primary & core hex colors based on the pilot's highest Pilot Skill level. When multiple skills are tied for highest level, falls back to the pilot's starting Trait Line primary gemstone color.

exports.name: isCheatModeActive
exports.doc: Returns `true` when developer progression bypass (`bypassProgressionGates`) is enabled on `state`.

exports.name: DoorwayAetherTransitionInfo
exports.doc: Descriptor for a cardinal doorway transition, including target coordinate, safety tier, and whether it enters Æther Fog.

exports.name: getDoorwayAetherTransitionInfo
exports.doc: Pure, non-mutating inspection of any cardinal doorway (`N`, `S`, `E`, `W`) in the active room. - Pyramid progression always follows: `SAFE (0) -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> SAFE (0)`. - `increasesDensity` is true whenever stepping through `dir` moves to a strictly deeper Æther depth (`nextDepth > currentDepth`). - `isLoopEntrance` is true when currently in a Safe room (`currentDepth === 0`) and `dir` enters an Æther Loop (`nextDepth === 1`).

exports.name: CHUNK_ROWS

exports.name: CHUNK_W_PX

exports.name: CHUNK_H_PX

exports.name: EXPANSE_TOTAL_ROWS

exports.name: SUNKEN_BOG_EXPANSE_ROOM_ID

exports.name: UnifiedBogRoomPlacement
exports.doc: Mapping entry anchoring a canonical M00 Bog room (`"rx,ry"`) onto the Unified Sunken Bog Expanse chunk grid (`cx`, `cy`).

exports.name: UNIFIED_BOG_ROOM_PLACEMENTS
exports.doc: Every authored RoomDefinition in M00 The Bog is placed directly onto the 26×18 chunk grid at `(startCx = 12 + rx * 3, startCy = 9 + ry * 3)` occupying a `2×2` chunk footprint (`20×18` tiles), separated by 1-chunk Set-Path Corridors (`stride = 3` chunks).

exports.name: UNIFIED_BOG_ROOM_BY_COORD
exports.doc: Lookup table mapping legacy M00 room coordinates (`"0,0"`..`"3,0"`) to their `UnifiedBogRoomPlacement`.

exports.name: SetPathCorridorSpec
exports.doc: Specification for a Set Path corridor chunk (`cx`, `cy`, `label`, `openings`, and lantern/hazard flags) in the Unified Bog Grid.

exports.name: SET_PATH_CORRIDOR_CHUNKS
exports.doc: Authored list of Set Path corridor chunks connecting the Drop-Pod Sanctuary (`cx=2,cy=5`) to the Eastern Causeway.

exports.name: SET_PATH_CORRIDOR_BY_CHUNK
exports.doc: Lookup map from chunk key `"cx,cy"` to its `SetPathCorridorSpec` along the Set Path.

exports.name: SET_PATH_SPINE_COORDS
exports.doc: Ordered list of `"cx,cy"` chunk coordinates forming the safe Set Path spine across the Sunken Bog.

exports.name: SET_PATH_SPINE_SET
exports.doc: Fast membership `Set` of `"cx,cy"` chunk keys belonging to the safe Set Path spine.

exports.name: getUnifiedBogRoomPlacement
exports.doc: Returns the `UnifiedBogRoomPlacement` for `roomCoord` if it is embedded in the Unified Sunken Bog Expanse.

exports.name: getUnifiedBogRoomAtChunk
exports.doc: Returns the `UnifiedBogRoomPlacement` occupying chunk `(cx, cy)` on the Unified Sunken Bog Expanse, or `undefined`.

exports.name: getUnifiedBogRoomAtPx
exports.doc: Resolves a world pixel position `(x, y)` in `px` on the Unified Sunken Bog Expanse to its enclosing `UnifiedBogRoomPlacement`.

exports.name: getEffectiveRoomCoord
exports.doc: Resolves the active authored RoomDefinition coordinate (e.g. `'-3,0'`, `'0,0'`, `'0,-2'`, `'1,0'`, `'3,0'`) when the pilot is standing inside that room node on the Unified Bog Grid, or `state.room` otherwise.

exports.name: convertBogRoomPosToUnifiedPx
exports.doc: Converts a local Bog room coordinate (`'-3,0'`, `'0,0'`, `'0,-2'`, `'1,0'`, `'2,1'`, `'3,0'`, etc.) and optional local room pixel `(localX, localY)` into world pixels `(x, y)` on the 26×18 Unified Bog Grid.

exports.name: ChunkFogMetrics
exports.doc: Computed Æther Fog depth (`0..4`), Manhattan distance from the Set Path, and deep-fog dungeon status for a chunk `(cx, cy)`.

exports.name: isChunkedExpanseRoom
exports.doc: Returns `true` if `roomId` uses the continuous `26x18` chunk-streaming expanse architecture.

exports.name: getChunkCoordsFromPx
exports.doc: Converts world pixel coordinates `(x, y)` in `px` into clamped chunk indices `{ cx, cy }` (`0..25`, `0..17`).

exports.name: makeChunkPersistenceKey
exports.doc: Formats chunk coordinates `(cx, cy)` into the canonical `"cx,cy"` persistence key.

exports.name: getChunkDistanceFromSetPath
exports.doc: Computes the minimum Manhattan chunk distance from `(cx, cy)` to any Set Path spine or landmark chunk.

exports.name: isDeepFogDungeonChunk

exports.name: computeChunkFogMetrics
exports.doc: Computes `ChunkFogMetrics` (fog depth, Set Path distance, and lantern suppression) for chunk `(cx, cy)` given `state`.

exports.name: CRAFTED_SUBMODULE_HARDWARE
exports.doc: Gem-Crafted Sub-Modules for Sensory A/B (`Head Mods 2-3`), Reactor Core (`Frame Mod 1`), and Leg Actuators (`Frame Mod 2`). Enforces the rule: Crafted mod parts have variable gem costs and at most 1 additional gem slot (`maxGemSlots: 1`), whereas looted standalone parts in the canonical catalogs have `1..3` gem slots. Internal sub-modules never grant exterior Armor Durability/Rating/Threshold; their bonuses map strictly to their physical domain.

exports.name: CANONICAL_HARDWARE_CATALOG

exports.name: findHardwareItemByNameOrId

Applies slot-adaptive physical domain bonuses and zero-sum trade-offs per Gem. Exterior Armor (`plating`, `head`, `arms`) receives Armor Durability/Rating/Threshold, while internal sub-modules (`actuators`, `optics`, `sensoryA`, `sensoryB`, `reactor`, `legs`) receive domain-accurate stats.

exports.name: resolveEquippedHardwareStats
exports.doc: Resolves the pilot's active Frame Plating, Dome Plate + Optics/Sensory, Aperture Plate + Actuators, Reactor Core, and Leg Actuators stats dynamically from equipped gear. Enforces physical intuition: ONLY exterior armor plating (`plating`, `head`, `arms`) and physical/ward shields grant Armor Threshold, Armor Rating, and Armor Durability.

exports.name: GEM_MOD_PREFIX_BY_ID
exports.doc: Canonical naming prefixes applied when a Gemstone is installed as the first mod on any equipment item. - Spinel -> Assault - Carnelian -> Heavy - Titanite -> Aegis - Demantoid -> Harmonic - Kyanite -> Arclight - Charoite -> Phantom - Moonstone -> Radiant - Rubellite -> Volatile - Hematite -> Ichor

exports.name: isCanonicalGemId
exports.doc: Type guard verifying whether a string is a canonical `GemId`.

exports.name: usesCustomSuffixBySemantics
exports.doc: Determines whether an equipment base name should receive `"Custom"` as a suffix (`<BaseName> Custom`) rather than a prefix (`Custom <BaseName>`) based on semantics: - Alphanumeric model designations (`N-55 Gladius`, `M-300 Hasta`, `WZ-800 Arclight Cannon`, `S-2 Turbine Khopesh`, `G341 Murmillio`) - Manufacturer/faction-coded hardware titles (`BWI ...`, `PNSY ...`, `VX ...`, `ARC ...`, `SANC ...`, `TI ...`, `RAD ...`, `NDS ...`, `BE ...`) - Equipment with explicit mark designations (`Mk.III`, `Mk.IV`, `Mk.V`, `Mk.VI`)

exports.name: parseEquipmentInstanceId
exports.doc: Parses any equipment identifier (`<baseId>`, `<baseId>::<gem1>+<gem2>`, or sparse `<baseId>::none+<gem2>`) into its base item ID, dense array of installed Gemstone mods, and positional `slotGems` array (`GemId | null`).

exports.name: buildEquipmentInstanceId
exports.doc: Constructs a deterministic composite equipment instance ID from a base item ID and either a dense array of `GemId`s or a positional slot array (`Array<GemId | null | undefined>`). Preserves `'none'` slot placeholders when later slots are populated before earlier slots.

exports.name: formatModifiedEquipmentName
exports.doc: Formats an equipment item's display name from its base name and installed Gemstones/Mods: - Uses semantic `"Custom"` placement: - Model designations & coded titles (`N-55 Gladius`, `BWI Bastion Frame Plating`) -> `<BaseName> Custom` - Standard weapon/armor nouns (`Camelot Longsword`, `Heater Shield`) -> `Custom <BaseName>` - 2nd+ mods append a Roman numeral tier count (`+II`, `+III`, e.g. `Custom Camelot Longsword +II` or `N-55 Gladius Custom +II`).

exports.name: COMBAT_TEMPO_CONSTANTS
exports.doc: Canonical Combat Tempo Constants anchored to a **Medium (`1.00×`)** deliberate tactical baseline (`40–50%` slower than arcade pace) with a **Moderate `±30%` spread** (`Light = +30%` faster rate / `0.77×` cycle duration; `Heavy = -30%` slower rate / `1.30×` cycle duration) and **`[0.70×, 1.30×]`** stacked multiplier caps.

exports.name: clampTempoMultiplier
exports.doc: Clamps any cumulative speed, cooldown, tell, or passive mobility multiplier into the canonical `[0.70, 1.30]` (`±30%`) band around the `1.00×` Medium baseline.

exports.doc: Classifies any weapon definition (across all 72 Customizable and 29 Magitech weapons) into its unified combat archetype using the 8 Weapon Classes and 9 Functional Types.

exports.name: buildWeaponUniqueComboSequence
exports.doc: Generates a weapon-unique, fluid, reload-free melee combo sequence (`2–5` steps) anchored to the **Medium (`0.45s/strike`)** deliberate tempo baseline with a **Moderate `±30%` band** (`Light = 0.35s/strike`, `Heavy = 0.59s/strike`).

exports.name: resolveSkillAmmoAndCharges
exports.doc: Resolves the appropriate multi-round salvo `ammoCount` and optional `internalCharges` for any ranged skill (`Slots 1..4` / Actions 2–5).

exports.name: normalizeWeaponCombatFunctions
exports.doc: Normalizes any `WeaponDefinition` to enforce the canonical combat overhaul, deliberate tempo rules, and strict **Base Combat Unit (`1× BCU = 54`)** parity across all 101 weapons: 1. `Bows`: Single-shot hold-to-charge weapons (`shotsPerChain = 1`, `isChargeable = true` on Slot 0, Medium draw = `1.15s` with `±30%` spread, Full Draw = `1.85×` base damage). 2. `Melee & Shields`: Never reload (`noReload = true`, `reloadDurationSec = 0`), fluid functional-type combo sequence anchored to Medium (`0.45s/strike`) with `±30%` spread, full chain normalized to BCU budget. 3. `Ranged Weapons`: 100% increase (`2×`) on Basic Attack (`Slot 0`) ammo (`shotsPerChain`), per-shot cadence decoupled from magazine size and anchored to Medium (`0.34s/shot` with `±30%` spread), reference salvo normalized to BCU budget, reload strictly on Slot 0 (`noReload = true` on Slots 1–4).

exports.name: isLauncherEquipment

exports.name: isAuxiliaryEquipment
exports.doc: Shields, Launchers, Quivers, and Catalysts are designated Auxiliaries (own Skill 4 and Skill 5). Note: Shields are 1H weapons that equip in Main or Side slot, whereas Launchers/Carriers equip in Aux (Back) slot only.

exports.name: isTwoHandWeapon

exports.name: canBypassTwoHandRestriction

exports.doc: Anatomical Weapon & Auxiliary Component Parts (`hilt`, `grip`, `blade`, `head`, `tip`, `focus`, `catalyst`, `actuator`, `sight`). Includes both Crafted parts (`origin: 'crafted'`, variable gem costs, `maxGemSlots: 0 | 1`) and Looted Standalone parts (`origin: 'looted'`, `maxGemSlots: 2 | 3`). Every part enforces the Zero-Sum Stat & Weight Law (`+Gain` vs `-Drawback` & `weightDelta`).

exports.name: getWeaponComponentSlots
exports.doc: Returns the 3 canonical anatomical component mod slots for any weapon or auxiliary item: - Melee (`hilt`, `grip`, `blade`, `head`, `tip`) - Ranged / Auxiliary (`grip`, `focus`, `catalyst`, `actuator`, `sight`)

exports.name: createStarterGemPouch
exports.doc: Executes `createStarterGemPouch` (create starter gem pouch) in `index.ts`.

exports.name: getWeaponSubtypeInfo
exports.doc: Executes `getWeaponSubtypeInfo` (get weapon subtype info) in `index.ts`. Returns the 8-category `WeaponCategory`, the shared functional weapon class (`functionalType`), and the `Custom` vs `Magitech` subtype so Customizable and Unique Magitech weapons are presented together inside their shared functional class.

exports.name: normalizeEquipmentInstanceKey
exports.doc: Resolves the canonical key for any equipment item (Weapon ID or Hardware ID) while preserving any `::<gems>` suffix.

exports.name: getEquipmentDisplayName
exports.doc: Returns the resolved display name for any equipment ID or name (including Gem-modified `+II` / `+III` variants).

exports.name: getEquipmentMaxModSlots
exports.doc: Computes the maximum number of Gem/Component mod slots (`1` to `3`) for any equipment or mod item: - **72 Customizable Weapons (`weaponTier === 'customizable'`)**: `3` anatomical component & gem slots. - **29 Unique Magitech Weapons (`weaponTier === 'unique'`)**: `1` Resonance Gem socket (fixed internal components). - **Crafted Mod Parts (`origin === 'crafted'`)**: Strictly capped at `1` additional gem slot (`maxGemSlots: 0 | 1`). - **Looted Standalone Armor & Hardware (`origin === 'looted'`)**: `1` to `3` gem slots depending on the item.

exports.name: createInitialEquipmentSlots
exports.doc: Executes `createInitialEquipmentSlots` (create initial equipment slots) in `index.ts`.

exports.name: isEquipmentUnlocked
exports.doc: Checks whether any equipment item (weapon, auxiliary, armor, reactor, or sensor) is unlocked/owned by the pilot. When `bypassProgressionGates` is enabled (or in `[-4,0]` Training Room), all items are available.

exports.name: getOwnedWeaponCount
exports.doc: Returns how many copies of a specific equipment instance (`<baseId>` or `<baseId>::<gems>`) the pilot owns.

exports.name: getOwnedEquipmentInstances
exports.doc: Returns all distinct owned equipment instance IDs (`baseId` and any `baseId::gem1+gem2` variants) matching a given base weapon or hardware item.

exports.name: installGemModOnEquipment
exports.doc: Installs a Gemstone Mod or Component Mod onto an owned equipment instance (`sourceInstanceId`) in ANY anatomical slot order (`slotIndex: 0 | 1 | 2` or `slotName`), consuming 1 copy of the source item and the required Gemstone(s) from inventory to produce a distinct renamed `Custom` item copy (`Custom <BaseName> [+II/+III]` or `<BaseName> Custom [+II/+III]`). Automatically updates any loadout slot where the last copy of `sourceInstanceId` was equipped.

exports.name: removeGemModFromEquipment
exports.doc: Removes/unsockets a modification or Gemstone from a specific slot index (`0`, `1`, or `2`) on an equipment instance in the Armory, updating the item instance in inventory and equipped slots.

exports.name: acquireAdditionalWeaponCopy
exports.doc: Grants or requisitions a second separate instance of a weapon so the pilot can enter Dual-Wield Paired Stance.

exports.name: getEffectiveMainGrip
exports.doc: Resolves the active Main Hand weapon grip ('1h' or '2h'). - 2H weapons (`isTwoHandOnlyWeapon`) are 2H-only unless overridden by a Feat, Unique, Legendary, or variable. - If no Side Hand is equipped (`!slot2`), the Main Hand is automatically 2H. - When Main Hand is 2H and Side Hand (`slot2`) is equipped, Side Hand is holstered at the hip while Launcher stays on the back (`slot3`).

exports.name: isSideWeaponHolstered
exports.doc: Returns true when a Side Hand weapon (`slot2`) is equipped while the Main Hand is in 2H grip. When holstered, the Side weapon stays in `slot2` (rendered sheathed/holstered at the hip) and the Back Launcher stays on the back (`slot3`).

exports.name: setMainWeaponGrip
exports.doc: Switches Main Hand weapon grip ('1h' <-> '2h') in the Equipment Screen. - 2H weapons cannot switch to 1H unless overridden by a Feat, Unique, Legendary, or versatile trait. - Switching to 2H holsters any equipped Side Hand weapon (`slot2` stays in `slot2`, holstered) while keeping the Launcher on the back (`slot3`). - Switching to 1H unholsters `slot2` into the active Side Hand (Launchers in `slot3` never move to `slot2`).

exports.name: unlockEquipmentItem
exports.doc: Unlocks any weapon, auxiliary, armor, reactor, or sensor into `state.equipmentSlots.unlockedEquipment`. If already unlocked, increments `ownedWeaponCounts` so additional copies can be modified or dual-wielded.

exports.name: unlockLevel2SecondaryWeapon
exports.doc: Unlocks the pilot's canonical Weapon Set 2 item (`startingWeapons[1]`) when reaching Level 2 (helping/resolving The Poe or salvaging Bedivere `[S]`).

exports.name: getWeaponActiveGemId
exports.doc: Resolves the primary active Gem modification (`Col 0..8`) for a given weapon/shield/quiver ID. First installed Gem determines the naming convention and visual sprite column.

exports.name: getWeaponGemCombatModifiers

exports.name: getWeaponGemVisuals

exports.name: modifyWeaponWithGem

exports.name: PlayerLightStatBreakdown
exports.doc: Structured stat breakdown for the pilot's derived Light stat (in tiles; base 5 = half one screen).

exports.name: computePlayerLightStatBreakdown
exports.doc: Computes the player's derived Light stat breakdown from base Light (`5.0` tiles) plus Feats, Hardware/Weapons/Items (e.g. Head Optics, Poe Lantern, Sensory Arrays), and active Skills/Spells. Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: computeEffectivePlayerLightTiles
exports.doc: Computes the player's effective Light stat in tiles (base 5 = half one screen), modified by Feats, Hardware, Items, Skills, and Spells. Does not mutate `state: OrionState`.

exports.name: adjustPlayerBaseLight
exports.doc: Applies a delta to the player's base Light stat (used by effects or sandbox tools). Mutates `state: OrionState` (`state.baseLight`).

exports.name: adjustEnemyBaseLight
exports.doc: Applies a delta to the enemy base Light / vision radius stat. Mutates `state: OrionState` (`state.enemyBaseLight` and active enemy `visionRadiusTiles`).

exports.name: toggleFeatNodeGemSocket
exports.doc: GEM USE 2 — FEAT NODE SOCKETING (Gems Removed from Inventory, Retained in Build, Refunded on Unsocket): Installing the required Discipline + Reactor Gems unlocks and activates the Feat Node. Unsocketing the Feat Node returns all retained gems back to the player's inventory. Enforces Per-Tier Feat Limits: Tier I: 6, Tier II: 5, Tier III: 4, Tier IV: 3, Tier V: 2.

exports.name: generateEquipmentModWithGems
exports.doc: GEM USE 3 — EQUIPMENT MOD GENERATION (Gems Spent; Mod Retained, Gems Are Not): Spends 1–2 Gems from inventory to permanently generate an Equipment Mod in `unlockedMods`.

exports.name: computeEffectiveLoadCapacity

exports.name: PlayerLoadMetrics

exports.name: computePlayerLoadMetrics
exports.doc: Computes the player's Total Weight Capacity (defined by Frame Plating + Frame Mods 1–3 + System Feats), Total Equipped Weight (Head + Arms + Frame + Weapons/Mods), and Load Percentage Bracket: - `0–30%` = `'light'` - `31–65%` = `'medium'` - `66–100%` = `'heavy'` - `>100%` = `'overloaded'`

exports.name: computeLoadPenalty
exports.doc: Percentage-Based Load Limit Penalty Table: - `0–30%` = Light (`mobilityMult: 1.08`, `heatMult: 0.9`, `swapTimeMult: 0.9`) - `31–65%` = Medium (`mobilityMult: 1.0`, `heatMult: 1.0`, `swapTimeMult: 1.0`) - `66–100%` = Heavy (`mobilityMult: 0.9`, `heatMult: 1.12`, `swapTimeMult: 1.18`) - `>100%` = Overloaded (`mobilityMult: 0.65`, `heatMult: 1.35`, `swapTimeMult: 1.45`, `stealthBroken: true`)

exports.name: evaluatePositionalHitQuality
exports.doc: Evaluates positional accuracy ("sweet-spot" vs "sour-spot") for a melee strike or projectile impact. Critical hits are a spatial accuracy variable rather than a random chance variable: - Spear / Lance tip (`0.68 <= rNorm <= 1.05` & tight centerline): `1.35x` damage, `+40%` armor bypass. - Hammer / Mace / Axe head (`0.60 <= rNorm <= 0.98`): `1.35x` damage, `+40%` armor bypass. - Sword / Blade upper cutting sweet-spot (`0.54 <= rNorm <= 0.92` & centered arc): `1.30x` damage, `+35%` armor bypass. - Haft / hilt / sour-spot (`rNorm < 0.42`): `0.72x` glancing damage, `-35%` armor bypass (enemy armor is 35% more effective).

exports.name: computeMomentumFraction
exports.doc: Computes forward momentum fraction `μ` (0 to 1) along a target/incoming directional axis. `μ = clamp(speed_toward_axis / reference_speed, 0, 1)` Returns `0` when stationary, moving away (`dot <= 0`), or moving perpendicular/sideways.

exports.name: computeEffectiveWeight
exports.doc: Computes Defender Effective Weight (`m_eff`) with directional charge bonus (§4, §6): `m_eff = m_defender × (1 + μ_defender)`

exports.name: computeStability
exports.doc: Computes Frame Stability (`S`, §5, OD-INR-06): Derived from frame weight + armor rating + hardware/feat/mod bonuses. Separate from weight `m` so a light frame can be built stable and a heavy frame is likely (not guaranteed) to be.

exports.name: computeMeleeImpulse
exports.doc: Computes Outgoing Melee Impulse (`J_melee`, §4): `attack_mass_eff = attack_weight + attacker_frame_weight × μ_attacker × commitment` `J_melee         = attack_mass_eff × attack_speed`

exports.name: computeRangedImpulse
exports.doc: Computes Outgoing Ranged Impulse (`J_ranged`, §2.6, §4, §9.6): `J_ranged = projectile_weight × projectile_speed` Explicitly includes NO shooter weight term.

exports.name: classifyInertiaOutcomeBand
exports.doc: Maps stability-reduced velocity change `Δv_eff` onto the 5 outcome bands (§4, §8, OD-INR-03): `'none' | 'flinch' | 'stagger' | 'knockback' | 'knockdown'`

exports.name: RecoilInertiaResolution

docs.title: Project Orion — World, Content & Base64 Asset Authoring Guide
docs.text:
# Project Orion — World, Content & Base64 Asset Authoring Guide

Welcome to the **Project Orion** authoring manual. The cartridge is built around **recursive module auto-discovery** (`import.meta.glob`), a **five-tier nested spatial hierarchy** (`Biomes → Rooms → Maps → Areas → Regions`), a **globally classless, hardware-driven build architecture (`v0.8`)**, and a **unified classical-mechanics Inertia & Stability physics engine (`inertia-v0.md`)**.

> **The Golden Rule of Orion Authoring:**
> Unless new content requires a brand-new engine mechanic or a new route entry in `KEY_NODE_ROUTES`, **you never edit engine files or `index.ts` registries**. Dropping a new `.ts` file into the appropriate `database/` subfolder automatically registers it on boot.

---

## 0. Quick-Jump Code Anchor Map (`[ORION-ANCHOR: ID]`)

Every critical registry, world-composer boundary, and engine hook in the codebase is tagged with a standardized `// [ORION-ANCHOR: <ID>]` comment block. Search for any anchor ID below to jump directly to the exact block of code to inspect or edit:

| Anchor Tag | File Path | Purpose & When to Edit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: TYPES-WORLD-HIERARCHY]` | `src/cartridges/orion/types/world.ts` | `BiomeDefinition` (`tileTypes`, `enemySpawnTypes`, `tileRules`, `tileAssets`), `TileDefinition`, `RoomDefinition`, `MapDefinition`, `AreaWikiDefinition`, and `RegionDefinition` schemas. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: U00-UNIVERSE-CATALOG]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/world/universe.ts` | The 20-World `u00` Universe catalog (`8 Major`, `7 Minor`, `5 Unstable`) and `specStatus: 'LOCKED' \| 'UNDEFINED'` world status flags. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: WORLD-GLOB-REGISTRY]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/world/index.ts` | Single polymorphic `import.meta.glob` scanner that auto-registers Regions, Areas, Maps, Rooms, Biomes, Tiles, Waystations, and Waygates. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: ASCII-CHAR-REGISTRY]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/world/index.ts` | Centralized ASCII character resolver (`getTileDefinition`, `resolveRoomEnemyTypeAtChar`) and `getMasterAsciiCharacterRegistry()` collision audit. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: ENEMY-GLOB-REGISTRY]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/enemies/index.ts` | Recursive auto-discovery for all Enemy, Boss, and NPC modules (`ENEMY_REGISTRY`, `CHAR_TO_ENEMY_TYPE`, `ENEMY_SPAWN_COLLISIONS`). |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: ENEMY-SPAWN-RESOLVER]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/enemies/index.ts` | `resolveEnemyTypeForChar(char, biomeEnemyMap)` and `getEnemyBySpawnChar` supporting biome-scoped spawn overrides. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: WORLD-KEY-ROUTES]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/world/roomLoader.ts` | Declarative `KEY_NODE_ROUTES` graph connecting authored `key` rooms (`"rx,ry"`) across cardinal directions with `routeTotal` general nodes. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: U00-ZONE-SEALS]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/world/worldTransitions.ts` | `getUndefinedZoneSealReason` enforcing `specStatus: 'UNDEFINED'` Æther Fog seals until a zone's canonical spec is unlocked. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: WORLD-COMPOSER-INIT]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/world/roomLoader.ts` | `assembleNestedWorld()` 5-tier world composer (`Region → Area → Map → Room`) and automatic cardinal doorway carver. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: AETHER-FOG-TOPOLOGY]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/world/worldTransitions.ts` | 5-node Æther Fog graph engine (`key`, `general`, `side`, `loop`, `end`) and `maxDepth = clvl + 1` loop scaling. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: ROOM-TRANSITION-GATE]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/world/worldTransitions.ts` | `transitionViaAetherDoor()` handling room-to-room doorway alignment, area banners, and dynamic enemy/feature spawning. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: WAYSTATION-WAYGATE-TRAVEL]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/world/worldTransitions.ts` | `fastTravelToWaystation()` and Colossal Waygate inter-region / inter-world teleportation & armor repair. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: CONTEXTUAL-LOOT-TABLES]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/world/worldPersistence.ts` | `ENEMY_EQUIPMENT_DROP_POOLS` and `resolveContextualEquipmentDrop()` hierarchical loot table resolution (`Enemy → Room → Area → Region`). |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: ENTITY-SPAWN-ROOM]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/entitySystem.ts` | `spawnRoomEnemies()` parsing `10 × 9` room ASCII grids using `resolveRoomEnemyTypeAtChar(char, state.biomeId)`. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: RENDER-CLUSTER-BAKE]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/render/worldRenderer.ts` | `bakeBiomeClusterTileset()` offscreen sub-tile micro-composer baking 20 separated `3×3` biome clusters (`ruins_tileset` & `bog_tileset`). |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: RENDER-VISION-LIGHTING]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/render/effectsRenderer.ts` | `resolveRoomLightingProfile()` dynamic vision radius (`baseLight` tiles), raycast wall/tree shadow occlusion, and static campfire/lantern light anchors. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: RENDER-POST-PROCESS]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/render/effectsRenderer.ts` | `drawDynamicLightingAndBloomPass()` 5-pass 2.5D lighting, water reflection, 1px outline, blade trail, and weather pipeline. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: PROG-LEVEL-SEQUENCE]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/progression/index.ts` | `LEVEL_UNLOCK_SEQUENCE` (`Levels 1–20`) onboarding & expression milestones. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: PROG-SKILL-SCALING]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/progression/index.ts` | `PILOT_SKILL_DEFINITIONS` (`6 Combat Discipline Skills`, `Lv 1–20`, funded by Discipline + Reactor Gemstones). |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: PROG-FEAT-SYNERGY]` | `src/cartridges/orion/database/progression/index.ts` | `doesPilotMeetFeatEquipmentRequirement()` classless hardware & weapon-family prerequisite verifier for all 97 Feats. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: COMBAT-ACTION-PAYLOAD]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/combat/skillExecution.ts` | `executeActionPayload()` resolving multi-source `[L]`/`[R]` actions, weapon skills, adaptive damage types, and support pulses. |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: COMBAT-DEFENSE-MATH]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/combat/damageSystem.ts` | `applyDamageToLayers()` Three Defense Layers resolution (`Layer 1 Shields → Layer 2 Armor → Layer 3 200 Frame HP`). |
| `[ORION-ANCHOR: INERTIA-PHYSICS-ENGINE]` | `src/cartridges/orion/systems/inertiaSystem.ts` | `resolveHitInertiaReaction()` & `applyRangedRecoilImpulse()` implementing `Δv = J / m_eff`, Stability `S` deadband/recovery, directional charge `μ`, and recoil restriction. |

---

## 1. Where to Start & Codebase Hierarchy Overview

All game data lives inside `src/cartridges/orion/database/`, domain types live in `src/cartridges/orion/types/`, and runtime systems and UI are cleanly modularized by responsibility:

```
src/cartridges/orion/
├── docs/                         # Consolidated Canonical Design & Authoring Docs
│   ├── INDEX.md                  # Narrative worldbuilding, Belldor stages & doc index
│   ├── CODE_RULES.md             # Engineering & AI authoring rules (commenting, modularity, memory/network safety)
│   ├── AUTHORING_GUIDE.md        # Technical architecture & content authoring manual
│   ├── EQUIPMENT_AND_FEATS.md    # 101 weapons (72 Custom + 29 Magitech across 8 Classes), hardware & 97 canonical feats
│   └── INERTIA_SYSTEM.md         # Inertia v0.1 physics & stability specification
│
├── types/                        # Domain-Organized TypeScript Schemas
│   ├── common.ts                 # Shared primitives, Base64SpriteConfig & PostProcessConfig
│   ├── combat.ts                 # DamageType, Three Defense Layers, Projectiles & Inertia
│   ├── equipment.ts              # Weapons, Chassis Hardware, Gemstones, Skills & Feats
│   ├── entities.ts               # Enemies, NPCs, Pickups, Particles & Floating Texts
│   ├── world.ts                  # [ORION-ANCHOR: TYPES-WORLD-HIERARCHY] 5-Tier World & Aether Fog
│   ├── state.ts                  # OrionState & OrionSaveSlot
│   └── index.ts                  # Barrel export re-exported by ../types.ts
│
├── database/                     # Strictly Self-Contained Content & Asset Entry Files
│   ├── world/                    # Spatial World -> Region -> Area -> Map (+ Rooms) Hierarchy
│   │   ├── index.ts              # [ORION-ANCHOR: WORLD-GLOB-REGISTRY] & [ORION-ANCHOR: ASCII-CHAR-REGISTRY]
│   │   ├── universe.ts           # [ORION-ANCHOR: U00-UNIVERSE-CATALOG] 20-World Catalog (8 Major, 7 Minor, 5 Unstable)
│   │   ├── belldor/              # 1. Belldor (Camelot) — Arthurian, canon (LOCKED)
│   │   ├── tyrranus/             # 2. Tyrranus (Greek/Roman, non-canon · UNDEFINED zone docs)
│   │   ├── global/               # Reusable procedural & inter-world templates
│   │   └── tiles/                # Shared tile & 2.5D prop definitions + embedded 16x16 base tiles
│   ├── enemies/                  # [ORION-ANCHOR: ENEMY-GLOB-REGISTRY] Self-contained Enemy, Boss & NPC modules
│   ├── items/                    # Consumables, 9 Gemstones, Currency & Quest Relics
│   ├── equipment/                # Slot-organized Weapons, Hardware, Frame Plating, Reactors & Utilities
│   ├── characters/               # 6 Classless Starting Loadout Kit profiles (Bastion, Fortress, Dawnforge, etc.)
│   └── progression/              # [ORION-ANCHOR: PROG-FEAT-SYNERGY] 97 Canonical Feats, 96-Node Constellation & Equipment Handling
│       ├── index.ts              # Canonical feats, gemstone economy, and progression helpers
│       └── featHandling.ts       # 96-node 6-arm hexagonal constellation coordinates & hybrid equipment prerequisite/handling evaluator
│
├── systems/                      # Modular Domain Engine Systems
│   ├── combat/                   # Modular Combat Subsystem
│   │   ├── combatHelpers.ts      # Aiming, target resolution, cooldowns & stance helpers
│   │   ├── damageSystem.ts       # [ORION-ANCHOR: COMBAT-DEFENSE-MATH] 3 Defense Layers + Inertia hit reaction
│   │   ├── projectileSystem.ts   # Projectile spawning, description-matched shapes (`bolt < pulse < wave`, `beam`, `arc`), homing & ray/crescent hits
│   │   ├── skillBehaviors.ts     # Enacted tactical skill movement, displacement (hook/bypass/shove), thrown/returning & lobbed mechanics
│   │   └── skillExecution.ts     # [ORION-ANCHOR: COMBAT-ACTION-PAYLOAD] 5-action execution, 2H side-holstering & Back Launcher (`auxActive`) ownership
│   ├── render/                   # Modular Render Subsystem
│   │   ├── spriteAtlasCache.ts   # Base64 image decoding, 1px outline baking & directional transforms
│   │   ├── worldRenderer.ts      # [ORION-ANCHOR: RENDER-CLUSTER-BAKE] 3x3 cluster auto-tiler, reflections & shadows

```

---

## 2. Authoring the 5-Tier World Hierarchy & Aether Fog Topology

### 2A. Aether Fog 5-Node Topology & Depth Progression (`[ORION-ANCHOR: AETHER-FOG-TOPOLOGY]`)
No outer room in Orion has a literal solid map border. Instead, `systems/world/worldTransitions.ts` routes cardinal doorways (`N`, `S`, `E`, `W`) through a dynamic 5-node Æther Fog graph with real-time HUD depth gauge and in-world environmental tells:
- **`key` Nodes**: Authored Points of Interest (Drop-Pod, Towns, Boss Sanctums, Waystations, Waygates) registered via `RoomDefinition` files and linked in `KEY_NODE_ROUTES` (`[ORION-ANCHOR: WORLD-KEY-ROUTES]`).
- **`general` Nodes**: Dynamically generated corridor chunks that advance route progress (`1/N .. N/N`) between connected `key` nodes when `routeTotal > 0` in `KEY_NODE_ROUTES`.
- **`side` Nodes**: Off-path branches extending from `general` or `key` nodes; they do **not** advance route progress and lead either to an `end` node or a `loop` node.
- **`end` Nodes**: Terminal single-exit pockets featuring rolled rewards (`loot_cache`, `mini_boss`, `secret_switch`, or `dead_end`).
- **`loop` Nodes (Depth `1 .. clvl + 1`)**: Going deeper into the Æther fog scales up to `maxDepth = clvl + 1`. Defeating a boss at `maxDepth` clears the fog (`clearAetherFogOnBossDefeat`) and returns the player to their anchor node on the main path.

---

### 2B. Master ASCII Tile, Doodad & Enemy Spawn Character Registry (`[ORION-ANCHOR: ASCII-CHAR-REGISTRY]`)

Every character in a `10 × 9` Room `grid` resolves through two passes:
1. **Terrain / Wall / Doodad Pass (`getTileDefinition(char, biomeId)`)**: Looks up `biome.tileTypes[char]` first, then falls back to global `TILE_REGISTRY[char]`, then defaults to `.` (`floor`) so enemy spawn characters automatically sit on walkable floor tiles.
2. **Enemy / NPC Spawn Pass (`resolveRoomEnemyTypeAtChar(char, biomeId)` at `[ORION-ANCHOR: ENTITY-SPAWN-ROOM]`)**: Looks up `biome.enemySpawnTypes?.[char]` first, then falls back to global `CHAR_TO_ENEMY_TYPE[char]`.

| *(Event)*| `lady_of_the_lake`| `enemies/belldor/lady_of_the_lake.ts`| `hostile` | Awakened via `awakenLadyOfTheLake()` in `0,-2` when carrying Bedivere's items. |

---

## 3. Inertia & Stability Physics System (`docs/INERTIA_SYSTEM.md`)

Project Orion uses a **weight-vs-weight classical mechanics Inertia & Stability model** (`src/cartridges/orion/systems/inertiaSystem.ts`) instead of a static poise pool:
- **Weight (`m`) & Directional Charge (`μ`)**: Controls physical displacement (`Δv = J / m_eff`, where `m_eff = m_defender × (1 + μ_defender)` and `μ` only applies when moving into the incoming hit).
- **Stability (`S`)**: Derived from frame weight + armor + leg stabilizers + feats; controls the shrug-off deadband (`k1·S`) and hit recovery speed (`Δv_eff / (k2·S)`).
- **Melee vs. Ranged Impulse (`J`)**: Melee impulse combines attack weight + attacker body weight × `μ_attacker` × commitment factor; Ranged impulse is strictly `projectile_weight × projectile_speed` (independent of shooter weight).
- **Ranged Recoil (`§7`)**: Uses the exact same impulse equation (`Δv_recoil = J_recoil / m_shooter_frame`) with deadband `k1·S`, so heavier and more stable frames suffer less movement restriction while firing heavy weapons.
- **No HUD Clutter by Default**: Inertia and Stability numbers are never shown on the default HUD; full physics telemetry is available in the `MECH STATUS` Satchel tab, and live HUD readouts only appear when the **Inertial Gyro-Telemetry Array** equipment mod is installed in Sensory B (configured in `ARMORY`).

docs.title: PROJECT ORION — CODE RULES
docs.text:
# PROJECT ORION — CODE RULES
### Rules for any AI or human writing Orion code (Gemini / AI Studio system instruction)
*Version: 0.1 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Status: Active*

---

## STATUS KEY

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| LOCKED | Stated by the project owner as required. Do not weaken without an explicit design session. |
| PROPOSED | Drafted wording or specifics. Pending owner confirmation. |
| DERIVED | Observed in the repo at the baseline commit (section 9). Match it. |
| UNDEFINED | Known gap. Ask before assuming. |

---

## 1. COMMENTING

- **License header.** Every `.ts` / `.tsx` file starts with exactly:
  ```ts
  /**
   * @license
   * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
   */
  ```
- **JSDoc on every exported function, type, interface and registry.** The first sentence says what it does and when it applies. Put identifiers, coordinates and concrete values in backticks (`"rx,ry"`, `10 x 9`, `cx=3..4`).
- **Comment the why and the invariants,** not what the line already says. Put units in names or comments (`px`, `tiles`, `ms`, `frames`).
- **Anchors.** Registries, world-composer boundaries and engine hooks carry a `// [ORION-ANCHOR: UPPER-KEBAB-ID]` comment. Never duplicate or delete an ID. A new anchor must be added to the anchor table in `docs/AUTHORING_GUIDE.md` in the same change.
- **Forbidden:** commented-out code, `TODO` / `FIXME` (record gaps as an Open Decision with an `OD-` id in the relevant doc), `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `any`.
- **Spec-driven code** cites its source section in the JSDoc (for example `mechanics-v1.md §9`).

---

## 2. MODULARITY

- **Content is data, one entity per file.** Enemies, weapons, items, equipment, rooms, maps and tiles live as separate files under `database/<domain>/` and are picked up by `import.meta.glob`. New content means a new file. Do not edit engine files or registry `index.ts` files to add content.
- **Engine code goes in its domain folder:** `types/`, `systems/combat/`, `systems/render/`, `systems/world/`, `ui/hud/`, `ui/satchel/`. A new system goes in the matching folder. Do not grow an existing large file.
- **Import direction:** `database/` imports only from `types/` and sibling data. `systems/` never imports from `ui/`.
- **Pure functions** for math and resolution. Anything that mutates game state takes `state: OrionState` explicitly and says so in its JSDoc.
- **No magic numbers.** Shared dimensions and tuning values live in `constants.ts` (`SCREEN_W`, `SCREEN_H`, room `COLS` / `ROWS`, and so on). Read it before using a number.
- **File size.** Plan a split before a file passes 1,000 lines.
- **Both HUD modes.** Any HUD feature states in its JSDoc whether it supports the React overlay HUD, the pixel canvas HUD, or both.

---

## 3. MEMORY SAFETY

- **Every listener, timer, frame request and subscription has a cleanup in the same module.** React code uses a `useEffect` cleanup return. Every `setTimeout` / `setInterval` / `requestAnimationFrame` has a matching `clear*` / `cancel*`.
- **No unbounded growth.** Any module-level `Map`, `Set`, array or cache has a size cap or a defined clearing event (room change, waystation rest, and so on). State the eviction rule in its JSDoc.
- **Reuse heavy objects.** Offscreen canvases, bitmaps and audio nodes are created once, reused, and released (set to `null`, or `width = 0` for canvases) when replaced.
- **No allocation in per-frame paths.** No new arrays, objects or closures inside update or draw loops. Reuse buffers.
- **Remove entities everywhere.** When an entity is removed from a list, remove it from every index, map and target reference that points to it.
- **Types.** No `any`. No non-null assertion (`!`) without a comment explaining why it is safe.

---

## 4. NETWORK SAFETY

- **The Orion cartridge makes no network calls today.** Do not add one unless the request explicitly asks for it.
- **If a network call is approved:**
  - Keep all network code in a single module.
  - HTTPS only, with a hard-coded host allowlist.
  - Use an `AbortController` timeout and a response size cap.
  - Treat every response as untrusted: validate its shape before use.
  - Never pass network data to `eval`, `Function` or `innerHTML`.
  - No tokens, keys or secrets in client code or in the repo.
  - The game must still work fully offline.
- **Persisted data (`localStorage`):**
  - Wrap every read and parse in `try` / `catch` and validate the result.
  - New save fields are optional, with defaults applied on load, so older saves still open.
  - Use the existing key constants. Never store credentials.

---

## 5. HOUSEKEEPING

- **Docs change in the same commit as the code.** A new anchor updates `docs/AUTHORING_GUIDE.md`. New equipment or feats update `docs/EQUIPMENT_AND_FEATS.md`. A new gap becomes an Open Decision with an `OD-` id.
- **Imports:** relative paths, alphabetized inside the braces, no unused imports or variables.
- **Formatting:** single quotes, two-space indent, trailing commas.
- **Naming:** `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` constants, `camelCase` functions, `PascalCase` types. File names follow the neighbors in the same folder.
- **Before handing back:** `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) passes and `npm run build` succeeds.
- **No leftovers:** no debug logging, no dead code, no stray files.

---

## 6. RESPONSE PROTOCOL

1. Restate the request in one line.
2. List the files you read.
3. Make the change, as complete files or exact diffs.
4. List files touched, new exports, and anything `UNVERIFIED`.
5. If a rule here conflicts with the request, say which rule and ask.

---

## 7. FILE STRUCTURE AND CONDENSING

- The current file layout is **not permanent**. As the codebase grows, files may be merged or condensed.
- Condensing must keep **wiki-like editability**: a reader can find the one place that owns a topic, edit it, and not touch anything else.
- Condensing **never removes a current function or export.**
- Anchors survive any move. Update the docs that name a moved file in the same commit.

---

## 8. DESIGN GUARDRAILS

*DERIVED — from the project docs. See `docs/` for the sources.*

- PvP and PvE share identical rules. No mode-specific balance tracks.
- Player stats are static. Progression unlocks slots and systems, never numbers.
- Damage, healing and feat values are expressed against the Base Combat Unit (`1× BCU = 54`).
- Every skill has a windup tell.

---

## 9. VERIFIED BASELINE (Updated 2026-11-12)

*DERIVED — re-check after major refactors.*

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `.ts` / `.tsx` files under `src/cartridges/orion` | 169 |
| License header on every file | Yes (169 of 169) |
| JSDoc blocks across `src/cartridges/orion` | 1,984 (100% exported symbols documented) |
| Files with no JSDoc at all | 0 |
| `// [ORION-ANCHOR: …]` anchors in code | 23 |
| `any`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `TODO`, `FIXME` | 0 |
| Network calls (`fetch`, XHR, WebSocket, `http(s)://` in code) | 0 |
| `addEventListener` / `removeEventListener` | 0 / 0 |
| `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` | Paired via tracked timer refs & unmount cleanup (`ui/OrionGameMenu.tsx`, `ui/settings/OrionSettingsPanel.tsx`) |
| `requestAnimationFrame` / `cancelAnimationFrame` | 4 / 4 (`ui/OrionHud.tsx`, `ui/satchel/SatchelCanvases.tsx`, `ui/satchel/AetherCosmosCanvas.tsx`) |
| Files over 1,000 lines | 21 (largest: `database/progression/index.ts`, 3,737) |
| Docs anchors missing from code | None (`0`) |
| Code anchors missing from docs | None (`0`) |

---

*CODE_RULES.md | Project Orion internal documentation*
*Version 0.1 — Initial rules for AI-assisted coding. Requirements from the owner; wording and specifics derived from the repo.*

# PROJECT ORION — EQUIPMENT & FEATS

## 1. WEAPONS (`101 CANONICAL WEAPONS` = `72 CUSTOMIZABLE` + `29 UNIQUE MAGITECH`)

### 1A. Eight Broad Weapon Classes, Nine Shared Functional Types & Two Subtypes (`LOCKED`)
All weapons in Project Orion are classified into **8 broad Weapon Classes** (`WeaponCategory`), each containing **9 shared Functional Weapon Types** (`WEAPON_FUNCTIONAL_TYPES_BY_CATEGORY`). Both **Custom** and **Magitech** weapons share the same functional weapon class (for example, `S-2 Turbine Khopesh` is a `Magitech` subtype of `Khopesh` under `Blades: Curved`, alongside the `Custom` `Khopesh`):
1. **`Shields`** (`Buckler` .. `Rhom` + `Aegis Charge Buckler`)
2. **`Bows`** (`Self Bow` .. `Great Bow` + `M-300 Hasta`, `M-450 Pilum`)
3. **`Casters`** (`Bolt Caster` .. `Stellar Caster` + `N-55 Gladius`, `B-25 Brushcutter`, `M-350 Mauler`, `RS-450 Radiant Projector`, `SV-12 Viper`, `SV-18 Serpent`, `SR-440 Shadowfang`, `WZ-800 Arclight Cannon`, `WZ-650 Prism Lance`, `WZ-450 Sparkstrike`, `ARC Conductor`, `CL-700 Sanctifier`, `CL-500 Absolution`, `CL-350 Litany`)
4. **`Spears`** (`Short Spear` .. `Lance` + `LS-900 Swordspear`, `HL-220 Lightburst Lance`, `WZ-200 Manacore Staff`)
5. **`Impact & Axes`** (`Cudgel` .. `Battle Axe` + `Siegebreaker`, `Hallowed Scepter`)
6. **`Blades: Curved`** (`Wakizashi` .. `Dadao` + `S-2 Turbine Khopesh`)
7. **`Blades: Straight`** (`Cinquedea` .. `Executioner Sword` + `TIG Edge`, `S-4 Whisper Blade`, `S-6 Phantom Edge`, `Grace Edge`)
8. **`Carriers & Munitions`** (`Bandolier` .. `Pangao` + `LN-1200 Avalanche`, `LG-950 Tomahawk`)

- **`Custom` Subtype (`weaponTier: 'customizable'` — 72 Archetypes + 5 Legacy Field Weapons)**: Have **3 Component & Gem Slots** (`maxModSlots: 3`) in the Armory Workbench (`Hilt / Grip / Stock`, `Blade / Head / Limbs`, `Counterweight / Focus / Payload`).
- **`Magitech` Subtype (`weaponTier: 'unique'` — 29 Unique Magitech Relics)**: Dissolved into the 8 Weapon Classes and their shared Functional Weapon Types while keeping their canonical names; feature **fixed internal components**, distinct movesets, and **1 Resonance Gem Socket** (`maxModSlots: 1`).
- **Weapon Combat Function Laws, Global `BCU = 54` Balance Parity & Anatomical Layering (`LOCKED`)**:
  - **Bows (`Bows` Class — Single-Shot Hold-to-Charge)**: All Bows (`Self Bow` .. `Great Bow`, `M-300 Hasta`, `M-450 Pilum`) are single-shot (`shotsPerChain: 1`, `isChargeable: true`) hold-to-charge weapons on `[X]`. Holding `[X]` draws the bow (`0% → 100%` over `maxChargeSec`), scaling Damage (`1.0× → 1.85×`), Projectile Velocity & Critical Sweet-Spot Range (`1.0× → 1.45×`), and Heat/Energy cost (`1.0× → 1.65×`). Releasing `[X]` fires the arrow and enters the single-arrow nock/reload cycle.
  - **Melee & Shield Weapons (`Spears`, `Impact & Axes`, `Blades: Curved`, `Blades: Straight`, `Shields` — Reload-Free Functional-Type Combos)**: Melee and Shield weapons never reload (`noReload: true`, `reloadDurationSec: 0`). Pressing or holding `[X]` chains through a fluid, functional-type-unique 2-to-5 step combo sequence (`buildWeaponUniqueComboSequence` in `database/equipment/weapons/comboChoreography.ts`) whose swing geometry (`swingStyle`: `slash` | `thrust` | `chop` | `bash` | `whirlwind`), per-step damage, range, arc, and lunge multipliers match each weapon's authored silhouette and description (e.g., `Khopesh` / `Shotel` / `Falx` hooked reach-around chops, `Wakizashi` / `Cinquedea` rapid multi-stab/slash flurries, `Pike` / `Lance` narrow high-reach thrusts, `Executioner Sword` / `Mallet` slow 2-step cleaves/slams, `Disc` / `Corona` rotary shield arcs). Pausing for the internal combo reset window (`comboResetWindowSec: 1.45s`) or completing the final combo finisher (`0.45s` Light / `0.58s` Medium / `0.75s` Heavy recovery) automatically resets the sequence to Step 1.
  - **Ranged Weapons & Description-Matched Projectile Hierarchy (`Bolts < Pulses < Waves`, `Beams`, `Arcs` — `resolveRangedBasicShotProfile` & `effectsRenderer.ts`)**:
    - All non-Bow ranged weapons feature doubled (`+100%` / `2×`) basic attack ammo (`shotsPerChain: 8..20`) and distinct per-type projectile silhouettes and collision physics (`ProjectileVisualShape` in `types/combat.ts`) that strictly match their authored weapon descriptions:
      - **Strict Size & Shape Hierarchy (`Bolts < Pulses < Waves`)**:
        - **Bolts (`visualShape: 'bolt'`, `radius: 2.1–2.6 px`)**: Fired by `Bolt Caster`, `N-55 Gladius`, `B-25 Brushcutter`, `SV-12 Viper`, `SV-18 Serpent`, `SR-440 Shadowfang`, and `M-300 Hasta`. Rendered as compact, high-velocity diamond/needle penetrators with slim slipstream wakes—the smallest and tightest projectile class.
        - **Pulses (`visualShape: 'pulse'`, `radius: 4.2 px`)**: Fired by `Pulse Caster`, `ARC Conductor`, and `CL-350 Litany`. ## 2. ARMOR / CORE FRAMES & HARDWARE DOMAIN RULES

### 2A. Physical Domain Separation, Load Brackets, Armory Workbench & Gem Socket Laws (`LOCKED`)
- **Exterior Armor vs. Internal Hardware**: Only **Dome Plates** (`slot: 'head'`), **Aperture Plates** (`slot: 'arms'`), **Frame Platings** (`slot: 'plating'`), and physical/ward **Shields** grant Armor (`armorDurability`, `armorRating`, `armorThreshold`). Internal sub-modules (**Optics**, **Sensory A/B**, **Actuators**, **Reactor Core**, **Leg Actuators**) never grant armor values; they strictly modify their mechanical domains (`lightBonus`, `accuracyMult`, `staggerDamageMult`, `tellDurationMult`, `attackMassBonus`, `stabilityBonus`, `heatVentMult`, `cooldownMult`, `moveSpeedMult`, `capacityBonus`).
- **Mech Doll `LOADOUT` vs. `ARMORY` Workbench**:
  - **`LOADOUT`**: Displays a central interactive **Mech Doll** surrounded by selectable anatomical hardpoint nodes (`Head Dome`, `Frame Plating`, `Arm Assembly`, `Leg Striders`, `Main Hand`, `Side Hand`, `Auxiliary Back Mount`, and `[L]`/`[R]` Trigger Binds) with a 4-action Slot Context Menu (`Equip / Swap`, `Unequip`, `Stance / Grip Toggle`, and `Modify in Armory`), a nested **3-tier Weapon Selector** (`8 Weapon Classes` ▸ `9 Shared Functional Weapon Types` ▸ `Custom / Magitech Subtypes`), and `128×128` technical schematics.
  - **`ARMORY`**: Houses all equipment modification systems—**Weapon Component Parts** (`3` slots on `Custom` weapons; locked on `Magitech` unique weapons), **Weapon Gem Sockets** (`3` slots on `Custom` weapons; `1` socket on `Magitech` unique weapons), **Internal Sub-Modules**, **Hardware Gem Sockets**, and **Action Modifications** (`Structure / Melee`, `Integration / Ranged`, `Mobility Kit`).
- **Non-Sequential Modification Slot Order & Semantic `Custom` Naming**:
  - Modifications and Gemstones can be installed, replaced, or removed in **any slot order** (`Slot 1`, `Slot 2`, or `Slot 3`) using positional slot encoding (`<baseId>::<slot1>+<slot2>+<slot3>` with `'none'` placeholders).
  - Modified items use semantic **`Custom`** placement (`formatModifiedEquipmentName`): **`Custom <BaseName>`** for standard weapon and armor nouns (e.g., `Custom Camelot Longsword`, `Custom Heater`) and **`<BaseName> Custom`** for alphanumeric model designations and manufacturer-coded hardware (e.g., `N-55 Gladius Custom`, `BWI Bastion Frame Plating Custom`), followed by **`+II`** or **`+III`** when 2 or 3 slots are populated.
- **Slot-Adaptive Gemstones**: Socketing a Gemstone into exterior armor modifies physical mitigation/durability/shielding, whereas socketing the same Gemstone into an internal sub-module adapts its bonus to that slot's physical function.
- **Crafted vs. Looted Mod Parts**: Mod parts crafted from Gemstones (`origin: 'crafted'`) have variable gem costs and at most `1` additional gem slot (`maxGemSlots <= 1`). Looted or standalone components (`origin: 'looted'`) have `1–3` gem slots (`maxGemSlots: 1..3`).
- **Zero-Sum Trade-Off Law**: Every stat increase carries a paired negative draw on another stat or equip weight (`drawbackDescription`).
- **Percentage Load Limit Brackets**: Total weight capacity is defined by Frame Plating base capacity (`84..140 WT`), Frame sub-mods (Reactor Core + Leg Actuators + Mobility Kit), and System Feats (`+22 WT` per step):
  - `0–30%` = **Light** (`+8%` Mobility, `-10%` Heat, `-10%` Swap Time) — *Rogue starts at `29%`*
  - `31–65%` = **Medium** (`1.0×` baseline) — *Warrior (`55%`), Cleric (`54%`), Dawnforge Guardian (`59%`), and Wizard (`54%`) start in Medium*
  - `66–100%` = **Heavy** (`-10%` Mobility, `+12%` Heat, `+18%` Swap Time) — *Marauder starts at `81%`*
  - `>100%` = **Overloaded** (`-35%` Mobility, `+35%` Heat, `+45%` Swap Time, stealth broken)

docs.text:
# Project Orion — Index

*A field guide to the Shattered Worlds, the road through Belldor, and the canonical documentation index*

---

## Documentation Directory (`src/cartridges/orion/docs/`)

| Document | Scope & Contents |
| --- | --- |
| **`docs/INDEX.md`** *(this file)* | Narrative worldbuilding, the Shattered Worlds, Belldor campaign stages (`M00 The Bog`, `Camelot Border Town`), starting loadout kits, and documentation map. |
| **`docs/CODE_RULES.md`** | Mandatory engineering rules for any human or AI authoring Orion code: Apache-2.0 license headers, JSDoc contracts, `[ORION-ANCHOR]` discipline, modularity, memory/network safety, and baseline verification. |
| **`docs/AUTHORING_GUIDE.md`** | Technical architecture, modular domain systems (`types/`, `systems/combat/`, `systems/render/`, `systems/world/`, `ui/hud/`, `ui/satchel/`), `[ORION-ANCHOR]` jump table, 5-tier world hierarchy, and Base64 asset recipes. |
| **`docs/EQUIPMENT_AND_FEATS.md`** | Full `v0.8` canonical catalog of 101 weapons (72 customizable across 8 categories + 29 unique magitech), 6 coreplates, 6 reactors, 18 aux/utility systems, 18 optics/sensors, 12 limb actuators, and 97 classless feats. |
| **`docs/INERTIA_SYSTEM.md`** | Working specification (`inertia-v0.md`) for the simplified classical mechanics Inertia & Stability model (`Δv = J / m_eff`, Stability `S`, directional charge `μ`, rock-paper-scissors triangle, and recoil). |

---

## The Short Version

The worlds were once linked by waygates. Then something was taken that should have stayed, and the links began to drift. You are a pilot: a being no world claims, immune to the æther between worlds, and able to bond with the war machines called mechs. Every faction wants you. None of them trust you.

This guide walks the road as it is currently planned, from your first step in the bog to the edge of what has been built. Past that point, the guide says **more to come**.

---

## Part I — The World

### The Waygates

At the heart of every known world stands a waygate, a colossal archway of stone, root and mineral that looks more like a canyon mouth than a building. There are no controls and no inscriptions. You walk through, and the gate reads your ætheric signature and carries you on. No one knows how it picks a destination. No one knows who built them. Scholars believe they were anchors that kept the worlds in alignment, and that belief fits what happened next.

### The Æther

Between the worlds lies the æther, an active and hostile medium. Living tissue that touches it disintegrates at once. The proof is infamous: on an interworld vessel, a single strand of an elven bride's hair crossed a flux-field breach, and she died instantly. Her death was taken for murder, and two elven clans fought an eight-year war before the truth came out.

Vessels can cross the æther only by holding a protective flux field around the hull. The æther can be resisted. It has never been tamed.

### The Mining Operation

A dwarven civilization once mined a rare crystal. Nothing happened at first. Then landscapes shifted without cause, ruins appeared where none had stood, and the stars stopped matching the records. The crystals were **tuning crystals**, calibration structures that kept the worlds synchronized.

> Worlds did not break. They drifted.

This drift is called **desynchronization**, and it is still happening.

### The Pilots

Pilots appeared only after the catastrophe. No world claims them, and no record of them exists before it. They can walk through the æther unprotected and bond with mechs at once. People say they are remnants of the catastrophe, or echoes, or walking fractures in reality. Nobody has proven anything. Factions recruit them anyway.

### The Fragmented Present

Distances between worlds now fluctuate. Some worlds drift closer, and others recede out of reach. The powers that thrive are the ones holding waygates, interworld vessels and strategic resources. The ones that struggle are cut off from their trade routes or stranded on drifting worlds. Some worlds have simply gone silent. War is constant.

---

## Part II — The Worlds

| World | Culture |
| --- | --- |
| **Belldor (Camelot)** | Arthurian knights and grail mythology |
| Tyrranus | Greek and Roman |
| Orion | Dwarven |
| Novarin | Orc |
| Chyme | Draconic |
| Golem | Desert |
| New Novarin | Elven |
| Sin | Underworld |

Seven **minor worlds** (Sylvis, Vox, Victor, Jager, Ferrous, Ebony, Ivory) and five **unstable worlds** (Aurora, Rhyme, Siren, Lennus, Malleus) also exist. The unstable worlds are in severe desynchronization, and reaching them may be intermittent or dangerous.

Your road begins on Belldor.

---

## Part III — Belldor

> **Belldor teaches you how to fight. Every other world tests whether you learned.**

Before the catastrophe, Camelot was a center of magic and governance with one of the largest waygates in the network. Now regions of it phase in and out of alignment, cities flicker between ruin and restoration, and its ruling authority is gone. Several factions fight over the waygate, and all of them recruit pilots.

The campaign on Belldor is built as a lesson. You are never handed a tool before the world gives you a reason to need it, and the numbers on your mech do not grow. Two pilots at the same stage are equally strong, and what separates them is what they choose to do.

### Choosing Your Starting Loadout Kit (`v0.8` Classless Spec)

Your mech is a modular war machine, and **Project Orion has no player-facing classes**. Six pre-configured **Starting Loadout Kits** are available at Pilot Creation so you begin with a coherent frame, reactor, and weapon pairing—none of them locks you in. Any pilot can equip any weapon, coreplate, utility system, or feat as long as they meet the hardware and gemstone requirements. See `docs/EQUIPMENT_AND_FEATS.md` for the full catalog of 101 weapons (72 customizable across 8 categories + 29 unique magitech), 6 coreplates, 6 reactors, 18 aux/utility systems, 18 optics/sensors, 12 limb actuators, and 97 feats.

| Starting Kit | Frame Model | Reactor | Starting Load Bracket | Lv.6 Tactical Utility (`Action 6`) | Starting Feats (`Tier I`) & Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Bastion Striker** | `PNSY W416` | Ichor | Medium (`55%`, `76/138 WT`) | PNSY D-0g Repair Drone | `Booster Evasion` + `Momentum Guard` · Frontline striker, aggressive, runs hot. |
| **Fortress Siege** | `RAD HAU` | Ichor | Heavy (`81%`, `150/186 WT`) | RAD R463 Fathomless System | `Siege Stability` + `Anchored Action` · Heavy siege artillery, high stability. |
| **Dawnforge Guardian** | `Trinity DE-14` | Mana | Medium (`59%`, `83/140 WT`) | TI Lightwell Recovery System | `Shield Charge` + `Stabilizer Pulse` · Defensive anchor, shields & cleave. |
| **Phantom Recon** | `VX Phantom` | Ether | Light (`29%`, `39/136 WT`) | VX Smoke Dispersal System | `Shadow Step` + `Phantom Strike` · Stealth striker, ambush & burst. |
| **Arclight Artillery** | `ARC Arclight` | Ether | Medium (`54%`, `75/140 WT`) | ARC Rift Anchor | `Beam Focus` + `Radiant Overflow` · Energy artillery, sustained beams. |
| **Sanctum Support** | `SANC Sanctum` | Mana | Medium (`54%`, `76/140 WT`) | SANC Radiant Ward Projector | `Reactive Healing` + `Empowered Blessing` · Support anchor, barrier triage. |

#### The Three Layers of a Build (`Pilot → Frame → Equipment`)
- **Pilot (`SKILLS & FEATS`)**: Created at New Game (`Starting Kit → Pilot Callsign → Level 1 in M00 The Bog`) and listed on the Load Game roster. Each starting kit begins with its primary **Combat Discipline** at `Lv 2` (`1` Gem invested) to unlock `Tier I` Feats. Six Combat Disciplines progress through gemstone investment (locked out during the `Levels 1–5` tutorial until `Level 6: Border Town Complete`) and unlock **Feat Tiers (`I–V`)**.
- **Frame (`SKILLS & FEATS`)**: **97 Canonical Feats** across Tiers I–V. Each starting kit begins with **2 pre-socketed `Tier I` Feats** matching its hardware and role. **System Feats** step up Load Capacity (`+22 WT` per step); **Interface Feats** tune combat behavior and weapon/hardware synergies within a fixed static budget. Feats are gated by Skill Tier, Gemstone sockets, and equipped Hardware/Weapon families—never by class—and can be unsocketed and refunded at any time.
- **Equipment (`LOADOUT`, `ARMORY` & `INVENTORY`)**:
  - **`LOADOUT` (`Mech Doll`)**: Organizes equipped hardware and ordnance around a central interactive **Mech Doll** surrounded by selectable anatomical hardpoint nodes (`Head Dome`, `Frame Plating`, `Arm Assembly`, `Leg Striders`, `Main Hand`, `Side Hand`, `Auxiliary Back Mount`, and `[L]`/`[R]` Trigger Binds) with a 4-action Slot Context Menu (`Equip / Swap`, `Unequip`, `Stance / Grip Toggle`, and `Modify in Armory`), a nested **3-tier Weapon Selector** (`8 Weapon Classes` ▸ `9 Shared Functional Weapon Types` ▸ `Custom` vs. `Magitech` Subtypes), and `128×128` technical schematics. **2H weapons** equip in the **Main Slot (`slot1`)** only unless overridden by a Feat, Unique, Legendary, or versatile trait; **1H weapons & Shields** equip in **Main (`slot1`)** or **Side (`slot2`)**; **Launchers (`Carriers & Munitions`)** equip in **Aux (`slot3`, Back Mount)** only and stay on the back while toggling active ownership of Skills 4 & 5 on `[L]`. When wielding a 2H weapon with a Side weapon equipped, the Side weapon stays holstered at the hip while the Launcher remains on the back.
  - **`ARMORY` (`Modification Workbench`)**: All modifications—**Weapon Component Parts** (`3` slots on `Custom` weapons; fixed parts + `1` gem socket on `Magitech` unique weapons), **Weapon Gem Sockets**, **Internal Sub-Modules** (`Optics`, `Sensory A/B`, `Actuators`, `Reactor Core`, `Leg Actuators`), **Hardware Gem Sockets**, and **Action Modifications** (`Structure / Melee`, `Integration / Ranged`, `Mobility Kit`)—are installed, replaced, or removed in the Armory in **any slot order** (`Slot 1`, `Slot 2`, or `Slot 3`).
  - **Semantic `Custom` Naming**: Modified equipment is named **`Custom <BaseName>`** for standard weapon/armor nouns (e.g., `Custom Camelot Longsword`, `Custom Heater`) or **`<BaseName> Custom`** for model designations and manufacturer-coded hardware (e.g., `N-55 Gladius Custom`, `BWI Bastion Frame Plating Custom`), appending **`+II`** or **`+III`** when 2 or 3 modification slots are populated.
  - **Physical Domain Separation + Zero-Sum Mods**: Only exterior plating (**Dome Plate**, **Aperture Plate**, **Frame Plating**) and physical/ward **Shields** grant Armor Durability, Rating, and Threshold. Internal sub-modules grant `0` Armor and instead govern their physical domains. Crafted mod parts cost variable Gemstones and have at most `1` additional gem slot (`maxGemSlots: 1`), whereas looted standalone parts have `1–3` gem slots. Every positive stat gain carries an explicit zero-sum weight or stat trade-off (`0–30%` Light, `31–65%` Medium, `66–100%` Heavy, `>100%` Overloaded).
- **Inertia & Stability (`docs/INERTIA_SYSTEM.md`)**: Hit reactions (`none`, `flinch`, `stagger`, `knockback`), hitstop freeze frames, and ranged recoil restriction are governed by the unified impulse-momentum model (`Δv = J / m_eff`) and frame Stability (`S`).

### The Æther Fog

Belldor does not hold still. Beyond the places that were built, the land frays into **æther fog**: stretches of the same ruined country that shift, fold back on themselves and refuse to stay mapped. It is what desynchronization feels like from the ground. Nothing in it is fixed, and a pilot who has been through it once cannot be sure the same road will be there twice. The fog is also what makes the world larger than it looks. There is no wall at the edge of the map, only more fog.

**Density.** The fog gets thicker the farther in you go, and everything gets worse with it. Enemies grow more aggressive, the mist hangs heavier, and the ground becomes harder to cross. Pilots are immune to the æther itself, so the æther is not what hurts you. The danger is the environment it creates, and nothing in it is safe.

**The path.** The fog is built around authored places: towns, boss sanctums, waystations and waygates. Between them lie corridors that carry you from one place to the next, with branches off to side pockets that hold a reward, a fight or a hidden switch. The game nudges you along the path, but you never have to follow it. You can wander the fog all day if you want to.

**Going deeper.** Some branches lead into the fog proper, and each room is one step deeper than the last. Until you reach the deepest room, you can always turn around and retrace your steps, and every room back toward the path is as safe as it was when you passed through. The deepest room is different. It holds a boss that must be cleared, and clearing it returns you to the last place you stood on the main path. The depth where the boss waits is not the same everywhere. A shallow pocket may bottom out after two or three rooms, and a deep one after five or more.

**The Lantern.** The Poe's gift is the one tool that reads the fog. It shows where the fog deepens and what is waiting beneath the water, and it never points you toward the story.

---

## Part IV — The Road Through Belldor

### Stage 1: The Bog (Levels 1–2)

You arrive in a drowned maze of fallen trees and the ruins of an old temple or monastery. The air is thick with æther. The water is not the æther's doing, but it is dangerous in its own right: **bog water is corrosive**. It eats armor, and it does not care who is standing in it. That includes the things hunting you. The marsh lies inside Belldor's æther fog, so the two overlap here, but they are separate things. The bog is not æther, and not every stretch of fog holds bog water.

**What lives here**

- **Orc pairs.** Orcs always come as a Warrior and a Scout. The Warrior is a shield-bearing brawler who closes distance and hits hard. The Scout stays back, shoots from range, and tries to slip away to heal if you hurt it. Kill the Scout first, but don't let the Warrior reach you.
- **The Bog Wurm.** A snake-like hybrid of machine and flesh, with glowing ætheric veins running through its mechanical parts. It hides invisible beneath the water, strikes first, and retreats to heal when hurt. The bog is its friend, and it knows it.

**The Poe.** Somewhere in the maze you will find a small floating lantern-spirit that calls itself "Poe." Every Poe says the same thing about itself, and they only manifest where the æther is thick. Helping it back to its lantern will earn you a gift. It reveals what hides beneath the water and where the fog grows deeper, and it will change how you fight the Wurm. Ignoring it or killing it is also allowed. The way out of the bog stays hidden until you deal with it one way or another.

**Bedivere.** Further on lies the body of a knight who was heading for the border town and never made it. He carries a **signet ring** and a **numbered list** of items that makes no sense yet. Taking the ring has consequences in the next zone. Leaving it has consequences too. The game will not explain the weight of that choice.

### Stage 2: Camelot Border Town (Levels 3–6)

The road out of the bog drops you at the outer edge of a large contested settlement, the gateway between orc territory and Camelot's interior. No one governs it, and no part of it is safe.

**The sickness.** Everyone here suffers from **grail sickness**. Some people are calm enough to trade. Some will turn on you if you linger. Some are feral and attack on sight. Which is which is not always obvious.

**The ring.** Knights' loyalists in town see anyone carrying Bedivere's ring as a grave robber. If you took it, loyalist merchants will not deal with you, and some will attack outright. Non-loyalists don't care either way. The ring is also your key to the dungeon subplot.

**The districts**

| District | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Outer Perimeter** | Collapsed walls, abandoned orc siege gear, burnt waystations. Where you arrive and the first line against invasion. |
| **Market District** | A half-working market where buildings flicker between intact and ruined every few seconds and the day-night cycle races. Container caches hold parts, consumables and blueprints. |
| **Barracks Quarter** | The former knight garrison, now a factional holdout. Strong fortifications, better loot, and the patrol routes of the three knights. |
| **Cathedral District** | Burnt grail tapestries, a defiled altar, bells that ring out of rhythm. The place to learn what the catastrophe did to Camelot. |

**Orc raids.** The orcs of the nearby encampment raid the town without warning. A war horn sounds, the screen pulses red, and the exit back to the bog is sealed until the raid is dealt with. During a raid **every NPC goes feral**. The orcs go after NPCs before they go after you, so you can fight for the town, stay out of it, or run for the dungeon and leave the market to be looted. If you save enough people, the survivors will remember it.

**The Three Knights**

| Knight | Fights as | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Percival**, Grail Knight | A guardian. A shield wall that has to be flanked or broken, and a charge that closes distance. | Protects his comrades. Recovers shields when badly hurt, so don't let up. |
| **Tristan**, Corrupted Ranger | A kiting archer. Volleys of arrows, smoke to escape corners, and a sight that finds you behind cover. | Fragile if you catch him. Punishes anyone who sits still. |
| **Bors**, Berserk Striker | A relentless brawler who grows stronger with every hit he lands. | Turns enraged at half health. His killing lunge is telegraphed, and deadly if you miss it. |

You can take them one at a time, or all at once for a better reward, a feat called **Knight's Oath**, which gives permanent bonus damage against Camelot's enemies.

**The Dungeon Door.** At the edge of the cathedral a stone staircase descends into mist, past carved grail symbols and flickering statues. This is the last gate before the Camelot waygate, and there are three planned ways to open it:

- **By force.** Defeat all three knights and take a Grail Fragment from each.
- **By exploration.** Find three hidden switches: one behind a desynchronizing wall in the market, one under the cathedral altar, and one in a secret armory room in the barracks.
- **By trust.** Earn the goodwill of the town through enough successful raid defenses. Carrying the ring makes this far harder.

Which of these will be live in the final game is still being decided.

### Stage 3: What Waits Below

Below the staircase lie lore, the key to the Camelot waygate, and the end of your first road. **Planned, but not yet designed.**

---

## Part V — Secrets

Some of what Belldor holds is not on the main road.

- **Bedivere's list.** Its items read as nonsense. They are scattered across more than one zone. Whoever collects them all and returns to the bog will find the water has been waiting. Something half machine and half serpent, an old name twisted by the æther, answers to the **Lady of the Lake**.
- **Hidden caches** in the border town hold blueprints, and every piece of gear in this game has to be found, crafted or earned.

---

## Part VI — After Belldor

By the time you are done here, you will have everything the game has to teach. Your frame, your weapons and your skills are all yours. From then on, progress is about **how** you fight and not how strong you are. A new weapon moves differently and does not hit harder, and different worlds ask different things of the same pilot.

**More to come:**

- **The Orc Encampment** where the raids begin.
- **The deep dungeon** beneath the border town, and the **Camelot waygate**.
- **Camelot's interior** beyond the gate.
- **The other worlds**: Tyrranus, Orion, Novarin, Chyme, Golem, New Novarin and Sin, plus the minor and unstable worlds.
- **Æther incursions.** Pilots can project their mechs across the æther into other pilots' worlds, as defenders or as attackers. The first incursion is an opt-in event somewhere after Belldor, and you can switch back out at any time with no penalty.
- **Queued 3v3 and 5v5 modes**, unlocked by exploration rather than level.
- **The truth about the pilots**, the waygates and the tuning crystals.

> The truth is not lost. It is unfolding.

---

*Project Orion — Index (`src/cartridges/orion/docs/INDEX.md`)*
